invariants: Invariant #15: src/lib/** and worker helpers receive their DB client explicitly — the extracted requireSettingsOwner takes (sql, request); route-helpers.ts must NOT import @/lib/db/server.
Invariant #2: the transactional outbox coupling is untouched — every terminal write stays in the SAME transaction as its outbox CAS, in the same statement order.

csv_ingest concurrency contract: every transaction that performs a contact_csv_uploads STATUS TRANSITION takes the per-business advisory lock as its FIRST statement, using the SAME key. This does NOT extend to every writer of the table — worker/jobs/account-offboarding/purge-stages.ts:256 hard-DELETEs by account_id without the lock, which is why the ingest 0-row case is reachable rather than impossible.
PII contract: the ingest lane and the batch executor never log names, emails, phones, notes, or raw CSV text — counts and closed enums only.

Terminal-write contract: every contact_csv_uploads terminal write carries the status='pending' predicate. Because only lock-holders change status, the predicate cannot change the outcome for a row that still exists; a 0-row result means the row is GONE (offboarding purge race), which completes the job silently today and MUST continue to.
Lock-order contract: in prepareBatch the accounts row lock is taken BEFORE the agent_runs row lock. evaluateBatchGate must therefore be called before the activeParent SELECT ... FOR UPDATE.
edge_cases: Ingest path terminal write matching 0 rows: REACHABLE, not impossible — the offboarding purge (purge-stages.ts:256) can delete the row between the pending read at ingest.ts:136 and the write at ingest.ts:155/167. Today the unguarded UPDATE matches 0 rows and the job completes normally; the refactor must preserve exactly that. Do NOT assert or throw here.
failed-hook and terminalizeUploadForInactiveSubscription terminal write matching 0 rows: legitimate no-op (lost race against a concurrent terminal write / completed job / purge) — must stay silent.

prepareBatch and constructBatch re-check the same gate (flag / subscription / offboarding) at two different times by design; sharing the check must NOT collapse them into one evaluation — construction's re-check is the load-bearing one.
The shared gate helper must preserve each caller's DIFFERENT failure posture: prepareBatch fails an activeParent only when one exists; constructBatch always fails preparation.parentRunId.
Calling evaluateBatchGate AFTER prepareBatch's activeParent SELECT ... FOR UPDATE would reverse the accounts->agent_runs lock order on a refactor-only branch. It must be called before.
requireSettingsOwner rejects an ?accountId query parameter BEFORE resolving the owner — the order is the guard, not an optimization.
Extracting requireSettingsOwner must not change the auto-approval route's impersonation branch, which runs AFTER the shared preamble and only on PATCH.

`pnpm ci:fallow` (--gate new-only) audits only CHANGED files and fails only on findings ATTRIBUTED AS INTRODUCED vs the origin/main snapshot. The batch-builder findings already exist in the base, so they stay 'inherited' and ci:fallow passes whether or not T5 happens. ci:fallow is a regression check (do not introduce NEW hotspots), never proof of decomposition — that is what the targeted complexity check in verification_commands is for.

`fallow health` rejects positional path arguments (exit 2), has no scoping flag, and exits 1 on ANY project finding. It can only be used via the JSON-plus-inline-check form in verification_commands; invoking it directly in a gate makes the gate permanently red.
